issues.legal_issue: A fresh acquisition declaration may be issued after the prescribed period for the original declaration has expired, without the initial acquisition notice lapsing, and compensation is assessed by reference to the fresh declaration.
material_facts: Land was notified for acquisition for planned development under the regional and town planning framework.
The original declaration was not made within the prescribed three-year period after publication of the initial notice.
The State issued a fresh declaration under the provision permitting a fresh declaration after expiry of that period.
issues.conclusion: The initial notice did not lapse merely because the original declaration was not made within three years. The fresh declaration was valid, and compensation was to be determined by reference to the market value on the date of that fresh declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 125 and 126(2) and (4) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, expiry of the period for making the original declaration permits a fresh declaration rather than extinguishing the acquisition notice; the fresh declaration date is the compensation valuation date. The Court relied on Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Dr. Hakimwadi Tenants Association, 1988 Supp SCC 55, which treated the fresh-date valuation as a safeguard for the landowner.

rule.if: planning_acquisition_proceeding and initial_acquisition_notice_published and original_declaration_period_expired and fresh_declaration_issued

predicates.planning_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding sought to acquire land for a planned public development purpose.
predicates.initial_acquisition_notice_published: The acquiring authority published an initial notice identifying land for acquisition.
predicates.original_declaration_period_expired: The period for making the declaration following the initial notice expired without that declaration being made.
predicates.fresh_declaration_issued: The government issued a new declaration to continue the acquisition after the original declaration period had expired.

issues.definition: When a planned acquisition has an initial notice, the original declaration period expires, and the government issues a fresh declaration, that declaration remains valid and compensation uses its date.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory deadline for making an acquisition award does not apply merely because substantive compensation principles from the general acquisition law apply to an acquisition under a separate enactment.
material_facts: The acquisition proceeded under a state enactment that expressly incorporated certain provisions of the general acquisition law.
The state enactment did not expressly incorporate the general law's award-making deadline, which was introduced by a later amendment.
In one appeal, the award had not been made within the period specified by that general-law deadline.
The Court accepted that compensation could be determined using the substantive principles governing compensation in the general acquisition law.
issues.conclusion: The award-making deadline in the general acquisition law did not apply to these acquisitions, and the failure to make an award within that period did not cause the acquisition notice to lapse. Applying substantive compensation principles did not import the separate procedural deadline.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished substantive compensation rules from procedural rules governing the time for making an award. It applied the compensation principles in section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, by necessary implication, but held that section 11A was not incorporated into the state enactment. Where provisions of an earlier enactment are incorporated, later amendments to that enactment do not become part of the incorporating enactment unless made applicable; incorporation differs from adoption by reference. The Court relied on Gauri Shankar Gaur v. State of U.P., 1994 (1) SCC 92.

rule.if: special_enactment_acquisition_proceeding and award_period_elapsed and selected_general_acquisition_provisions_incorporated and award_deadline_not_incorporated

predicates.special_enactment_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding seeks acquisition under a separate enactment rather than directly under the general acquisition law.
predicates.award_period_elapsed: The period allowed for making an award under the general acquisition law passed before an award was made.
predicates.selected_general_acquisition_provisions_: The separate enactment expressly made some provisions of the general acquisition law part of its own scheme.
predicates.award_deadline_not_incorporated: The separate enactment did not expressly make the general law's award-making deadline applicable to its acquisitions.

issues.definition: When an acquisition under a separate enactment misses the general law's award period, incorporation of selected general-law provisions without its award deadline does not make the acquisition lapse.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment governing acquisition proceedings applies to proceedings initiated after the amendment came into force, as well as to proceedings that were already pending.
material_facts: The state enactment was amended to provide for fresh acquisition declarations after the original declaration period expired.
The issue included proceedings initiated after the amendment came into force.
The Court agreed with the Full Bench view that the amendment applied to later proceedings as well as pending proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The amendment applied to proceedings initiated after it came into force and was not confined to proceedings already pending on that date.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read the opening language and scheme of the fresh-declaration provision as applying the amendment to later as well as pending proceedings. It agreed with the reasoning and conclusion in Shiorani v. State of Maharashtra, 1994 Mh.L.J. 1821.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding_under_amended_fra: The acquisition proceeding is governed by a statutory framework that has been amended to permit a fresh declaration.
predicates.proceeding_initiated_after_amendment: The acquisition proceeding began after the amendment came into force.

issues.definition: A proceeding initiated after an amendment to the acquisition framework is governed by that amendment.
